races.name: Cumbria Grand Maiden Hurdle Race (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Gambino
runners_data.note: Harry Skelton's mount has a progressive profile with a win and two places from five runs, showing best on Good and Standard surfaces, and sitting prominent behind an uncontested Manhatane is exactly the tactical setup this horse needs at Cartmel.|

runners_data.name: Kind Of Kiss
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up performer with a mediocre flat record — 0 wins, 0 places from 14 Good-ground runs — who has been placed into midfield on the map simply because the field is packed with closers; tongue-tie noted and Sam England's 2/11 trainer strike rate over 14 days provides limited support.|

runners_data.name: Masekela
runners_data.note: Brian Hughes links up with James Moffatt (who also saddles Manhatane) and brings the most relevant sim-going experience of any runner with 4 places from 10 Good-ground runs; despite being a natural hold-up horse shifted forward on the map, Hughes is savvy enough to find a practical position and this horse has a realistic each-way profile.|

runners_data.name: Scopic
runners_data.note: Ran 37 days ago and all three hurdle starts on Good ground have produced finishes of 6th, 8th, and a pull-up — the form string offers nothing compelling, and as a genuine closer in a race that is unlikely to be run at a truly honest tempo, it faces a structural disadvantage.|

runners_data.name: Speed For Fun
runners_data.note: The Willie Mullins representative ridden by his son is an immediate unknown over hurdles having fallen on debut over timber; the flat form shows mid-table finishes at best but Mullins's 4/26 14-day trainer record reminds you that this yard operates at volume, and the horse's class ceiling is genuinely unclear.|

runners_data.name: Steps In Time
runners_data.note: Ran 37 days ago with a pull-up and a 6th from two recent hurdle starts, and Good-ground form from 11 runs yields just 1 place and no wins; Philip Kirby's 2/16 trainer strike rate over 14 days is modest, and Joe Williamson's booking offers no particular angle.|

runners_data.name: Order Another One
runners_data.note: Ran just two days ago — the most significant flag here — over a 5-furlong longer trip and finishes outside the money on both hurdle starts at Cartmel; the 7lb allowance via the lighter weight helps marginally but returning so quickly over a shorter trip looks like stable management rather than a winning move.|

runners_data.name: Manhatane
runners_data.note: The race's sole front-runner, trained by James Moffatt and ridden by 7lb claimer Leah Noreci, has run twice over longer trips (22f) and is stepping down to 2m1f; the lack of any pace rival means it will control the race, but whether a young claimer can judge fractions correctly around Cartmel's unique circuit is the key race question.|

races.paceDynamic: Manhatane is the sole confirmed front-runner in this nine-runner maiden hurdle and, ridden by a 7lb claimer in Leah Noreci, is likely to stride into a clear lead from the off at Cartmel's tight, turning track over 2m1f on Good ground. With no credible challenger for the lead, Manhatane will control tempo entirely, setting a sustainable gallop that suits those travelling prominently behind — Gambino, ridden by Harry Skelton, is the most natural beneficiary as a genuine prominent type with recent Good-ground form. The field contains a cluster of horses — Masekela, Kind Of Kiss, and Destination Unknown — who are true hold-up types but cannot all secure their natural position at the rear given how few runners will genuinely press forward, and have been redistributed to midfield on the map; their effective lack of cover from a true pace injection means their finishing kicks may be blunted. This race shape strongly favours prominent racers who can sit close to Manhatane's uncontested lead, travel comfortably on Good ground, and pounce approaching the final hurdle — Gambino's profile fits that template precisely.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Manhatane Leads, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Manhatane dictates an uncontested, measured gallop and a prominent tracker pounces before the last.
scenarios.body: Manhatane sets a controlled pace around Cartmel's turning circuit, with Gambino sitting second or third and producing a clean jump at the final flight to assert; the Good ground and straightforward lead-track dynamic plays directly into the hands of those racing within striking distance throughout.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Midfield Lands
scenarios.trigger: If Manhatane goes off too fast under inexperienced handling and weakens before the final flight, gifting the race to a chasing midfield horse.
scenarios.body: A 7lb claimer setting solo fractions at Cartmel can misjudge the pace on a tight track, and a collapse in the lead would allow those sitting off the pace in midfield to pick up the pieces; Masekela and Kind Of Kiss, though racing out of their ideal hold-up role, are closest to a true finishing position in this version of events.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Storms Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong throughout and genuine closer Order Another One or Scopic threads through late.
scenarios.body: A hot early gallop from Manhatane, pushed harder than expected, could produce a truly run race that rewards horses finishing hard from off the pace; Scopic and Order Another One have the profile of genuine hold-up types, though neither has convincing form to inspire confidence at this trip and track.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Market Mover Upsets
scenarios.trigger: If Speed For Fun, the Mullins-trained unknown quantity, shows a class edge that flat form hints at and tracks up to win smoothly.
scenarios.body: W P Mullins with Mr P W Mullins aboard carries significant market authority even on debut over hurdles, and if Speed For Fun travels like a classier horse throughout it could overpower this field with minimal effort; the key unknown is whether hurdling technique holds on Good ground on debut over timber.

watchPoints.text: Manhatane — watch whether Leah Noreci (7lb claimer) over-races or misjudges fractions on Cartmel's tight circuit; if the pace collapses or runs too hot, the entire race shape changes.
Gambino — watch market moves at the off; Harry Skelton with the ideal tactical seat directly behind an uncontested leader is the shape this horse was made for, and any drift would be telling.
Masekela — Brian Hughes riding for the same Moffatt yard as Manhatane; watch for any stable information angle and whether Hughes opts to track his stablemate or take a wider position.
Order Another One — ran only two days ago, worth watching in the parade ring and early in the race for any signs of fatigue; a horse returning this quickly rarely performs at peak.
Speed For Fun — an unknown quantity on hurdles debut for Mullins; watch the market from opening show to off-time, as any significant support would suggest stable confidence about jumping ability.

races.name: Molson Coors Handicap Hurdle Race (Div II)

runners_data.name: Fairlawn Skipper
runners_data.note: Shane Fenelon (5lb claim) partners this hold-up operator who has placed three times in similar going (6/9 sim-going record), but the tight Cartmel track and a tendency to race far back makes finishing runs difficult when pace is limited; 44 days off is not a concern given the form shows consistency.

runners_data.name: Fourofakind
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up horse who has been off 120 days and wears headgear (p) — the long absence is the main concern, and all five recent runs have come over 20f meaning this step up to 2m6f is a significant trip question; Sean Quinlan's booking is positive but the fitness query looms large.

runners_data.name: Lelantos
runners_data.note: Nicky Henderson's 10-year-old sets out as the confirmed pace-maker here and won over this course and distance, but the STYLE_FIT flag (0.92) signals this is not his natural race shape — his age and modest trainer 14-day strike rate (0/4) suggest he is best used as a pace reference point rather than a win anchor.

runners_data.name: Les's Destiny Star
runners_data.note: Callum Bewley takes over on this prominent racer who wears a tongue-tie and has a decent sim-going mark (4/10); trainer Ewan Whillans is in form at 3/16 over 14 days, and the horse has placed at 24f in soft, so the Good ground and slight trip extension should not be prohibitive — two pulled-up runs in recent form are the flag.

runners_data.name: Matoury
runners_data.note: William Maggs (3lb claim) rides this progressive prominent type who has won his last two starts over 23f on Good ground, compiling a standout sim-going record of 12/15 with 3W9P; the step to 2m6f is the only uncertainty, but his trajectory and fresh conditions make him the most compelling form horse in the race.

runners_data.name: Top Flight Century
runners_data.note: A prominent racer dropping from OR=90 who has been consistent at 20f on Good (12/15 sim-going) though Joshua Thompson's 5lb claim partially offsets the weight; five-year-old with a yard that has hit only 1 run in 14 days — limited trainer momentum but young horse still on an upward curve.

runners_data.name: Masterminding
runners_data.note: Leah Noreci's 7lb claim gives this hold-up type a meaningful weight break; placed in both recent Good-ground starts over 22f and the sim-going record is solid (11/15 0W2P), suggesting a reliable if win-shy profile — will need the pace to collapse to get competitive from his rearward position.

runners_data.name: Katzoff
runners_data.note: Dan Skelton's leading handler angle (6/25 T14) is notable, and Harry Skelton's booking adds class to the partnership, but this is a natural rear-runner whose true hold-up style has been shifted forward on the map — the redistribution tag means the Skelton combination may not get the run of the race that typically fuels their strike rate; form string shows limited recent effectiveness.

runners_data.name: Zuul
runners_data.note: Rebecca Menzies has a quiet 14-day record (0/14) and this hold-up type wears headgear (tp) — four placed efforts from 14 sim-going runs suggest a consistently honest horse who rarely wins; Ellis Collier's 5lb claim helps the weight, but the redistribution from true hold-up to mapped midfield means he will race slightly out of comfort zone in what is expected to be a steadily-run affair.

races.paceDynamic: Lelantos is the lone confirmed front-runner here and, with no natural rival to push him along, he should be able to dictate from the front at a controlled, sustainable gallop over this 2m6f trip on Good ground at Cartmel. Behind him, Les's Destiny Star, Matoury, and Top Flight Century will all press for prominent positions, creating a competitive early scramble for the favoured spots just off the lead. The field contains more hold-up and prominent types than can realistically settle into their preferred positions — Katzoff and Zuul are genuine rear-runners who are effectively mapped into midfield because the pace bias pushes true closers further forward than ideal, which significantly dilutes their threat. This pace shape — a single unhurried front-runner with a cluster of prominent racers immediately behind — overwhelmingly favours horses who can travel in the first four and attack from a close-up position from the second-last flight, rather than those trying to make up ground from off the pace on a tight, turning track like Cartmel.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Lelantos Controls, Prominent Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If Lelantos gets a clean lead and sets an honest but unspectacular gallop, allowing the prominent horses just off him to travel comfortably into contention.
scenarios.body: Lelantos dictates the fractions from the front, the race stays compact, and the horses sitting second or third from the second-last flight are best placed to pounce; Cartmel's tight, turning layout rewards those who never lose contact with the pace.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Matoury Dominates, Confirms Form
scenarios.trigger: If Matoury's sharp recent form (two wins in 23f on Good) translates directly and his claims at a longer trip prove valid.
scenarios.body: Fresh off back-to-back wins and with the best recent form record in the field on similar going, Matoury's W/P ratio of 3W9P at 12/15 sim-going runs marks him as the standout live contender if the moderate pace suits a front-running type hitting the top of his form.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Hold-Up Gets In
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent group quicken early and seriously test Lelantos, causing a messy, fast-run race that drains the leaders and opens the door for a late finisher.
scenarios.body: A scenario that depends on Katzoff or Zuul closing from the rear is inherently limited by their redistribution — both are true hold-up horses who will be positioned further forward than ideal, blunting their finishing kick; nonetheless a genuinely strong pace could allow Masterminding or Fairlawn Skipper to stay on past tiring rivals.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Front-Runner Wires Field
scenarios.trigger: If Lelantos is given a soft enough lead that he simply outstays every rival who tries to close on the testing Cartmel circuit.
scenarios.body: At 10 years old with a win over this exact course and distance, Lelantos has the track craft to make his lead count if the prominent horses over-exert themselves chasing; the risk is that his OR of 95 and a field of improving types makes a wire-to-wire win the least likely of the front-end outcomes rather than the most.

watchPoints.text: Matoury is the one to watch as a form horse on a hat-trick bid — if William Maggs slots him into his natural prominent position early, his two recent Good-ground wins make him the primary threat to the entire field.

Lelantos's ability to secure an uncontested lead without pressure from Les's Destiny Star and Top Flight Century is the race's key structural question — if those three jostle aggressively for the front positions it fundamentally changes how the race is run.

Katzoff and Zuul, both mapped out of their natural hold-up roles, should be monitored at the start — if either is forced to race more prominently than preferred, their chance of landing a winning blow from off the pace diminishes further.

Fourofakind's 120-day absence is the longest in the field and Sean Quinlan should be watched in the early stages to see whether the horse travels with any fluency — a sluggish reappearance would confirm fitness is the limiting factor.

Cartmel's tight turning track historically makes it very difficult to make up ground from off the pace in a moderate-gallop handicap hurdle — watch for the first three home all likely to have been prominent from an early stage.

races.name: Furness Building Society Handicap Hurdle Race

runners_data.name: Scots Poet
runners_data.note: Three course-and-distance wins on Good ground underpins strong claims; tongue bar noted; returned just eight days ago in winning form and his natural front-running role is perfectly suited to the single-pace shape this race is expected to take.

runners_data.name: Big Gypsy King
runners_data.note: A four-year-old lightly framed for this company, his sole hurdles win came over 17f on Good and he is held up naturally, though modest pace could allow him to travel closer than usual; 7lb claimer Leah Noreci adding inexperience to an already untested profile.

runners_data.name: Zamond
runners_data.note: Consistent performer on Good ground with two recent placings at 17f; prominent style makes him the natural default challenger to Scots Poet and Donald McCain's yard has been in decent form over the 14-day window with one winner from eleven runners.

runners_data.name: Raffles Nobu
runners_data.note: Genuine form to recommend him — a win and a place at 18f on Good in recent outings — and the tongue-bar is a positive flag; however, his natural closing style means he genuinely needs a fast pace that this race shape is unlikely to generate, which tempers enthusiasm significantly.

runners_data.name: Interchangeable
runners_data.note: Five runs in a row without troubling the judge, with form figures of 603-65 telling a consistent story of mid-pack finishes; amateur rider John Dixon (7lb claim) trains and rides, and while the trip and going are not concerns, the horse lacks the tactical speed to exploit a slow pace.

runners_data.name: Assorda
runners_data.note: Six runs on Good ground and six losing efforts, with finishing positions of 6-6-5-6-6 painting a bleak picture; a true hold-up type who has found himself mapped to midfield due to the glut of closers in this field, but the real issue is a form profile that offers no encouragement at this level.

runners_data.name: Ambassador
runners_data.note: Nine-year-old veteran wearing a visor, and the 47-day absence plus a recent form string of 6P68-9 raises serious questions about current well-being; one of four natural closers who will struggle to get their preferred position and to generate a winning run from the rear at the same time.

runners_data.name: Mr Globalist
runners_data.note: Ran just two days ago, which is an immediate flag regardless of conditions; consistent placer on Good ground (three 3rds and two 4ths in last five), visor-fitted, and his trainer-jockey combination (Lizzie and Sean Quinlan) is a compact operation — but freshness must be questioned after such a rapid turnaround.

races.paceDynamic: Scots Poet is the sole confirmed front-runner in this eight-runner field and, with no genuine rival to press him from the front, he is likely to control proceedings at a sensible, sustainable gallop around Cartmel's tight 2m1f circuit. Zamond is the only other horse mapped prominently and will likely sit in behind, meaning the early pace is unlikely to be frantic — Scots Poet can dictate terms and preserve energy into the home straight. This controlled, single-paced shape strongly favours those who can sit close to the tempo and kick from the front or just off it, rather than horses needing a genuine strong gallop to close into. The field contains a significant surplus of hold-up types — Raffles Nobu, Assorda, Ambassador, and Mr Globalist are all natural closers redistributed to midfield on the map, and in a race where Scots Poet sets a measured pace, those four are unlikely to generate the strong gallop they need to deliver their finishing kicks effectively; the race shape most favours prominent-to-front profiles.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Scots Poet Dictates Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Scots Poet leads from the front uncontested and sets a measured, controlled gallop that denies the hold-up horses a true test.
scenarios.body: Scots Poet uses his recent course-and-distance winning form (three wins at 16f on Good) to bowl along at his own pace and prove too strong, with Zamond the likeliest to sit close enough to challenge.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Duo Fight It Out
scenarios.trigger: If Zamond tracks Scots Poet closely and applies enough mid-race pressure to force a genuine duel in the final circuit.
scenarios.body: The tempo lifts sufficiently to stretch the field, making it a two-horse battle between the lead pair from the final hurdle, with Zamond's consistent course-form (two places at 17f Good) enabling him to outlast.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Pounces Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong enough to suit a horse held up, and one of the redistributed closers manages to find clear daylight.
scenarios.body: Raffles Nobu is the most likely candidate given recent form (1-2 at 18f Good) and a tongue-tie sharpening his jumping, but the redistribution tag reflects how unlikely this scenario is to materialise given the modest anticipated gallop.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Modest Pace Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If the field crawls early and the race degenerates into a sprint finish where lower-rated horses with fresh legs capitalise.
scenarios.body: Mr Globalist (2d since last run, consistent placing form on Good) or Interchangeable could benefit from a sprint-up scenario, though both sit well down the weights and lack the form ceiling to beat the principals.

watchPoints.text: Scots Poet sets every fraction from the front unchallenged — if he bowls along without pressure and jumps cleanly, his three course-and-distance wins on identical going make him the one to beat on pace shape alone.

Zamond is the only horse with both the prominent style and the Good-ground course form to sit close enough to Scots Poet to challenge; watch whether Theo Gillard elects to press or give him a soft lead.

Raffles Nobu's redistribution from hold-up to midfield means Jack Quinlan may find himself in an unnatural early position — watch the first few flights to see whether he settles or over-races, as that will determine whether his closing kick can be deployed.

Mr Globalist ran just two days ago under Sean Quinlan — watch for any signs of fatigue or reluctance in the paddock, as a rapid turnaround on Good ground for a hold-up horse in a slow-pace race is a notably unfavourable combination of factors.

Big Gypsy King is the only four-year-old in the field and has a flat/AW background (three starts at Southwell and Carlisle on Standard), so his jumping fluency over hurdles on a tight Cartmel circuit with Good ground is worth monitoring from the outset.

races.name: RF Miller & Co Handicap Steeple Chase (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Stratagem
runners_data.note: Two wins over 26f on Good ground are directly relevant here; ridden by 7lb claimer Mr J P Murray who reduces his weight burden, and tp headgear suggests he is at his most reliable when on a handy lead — STYLE_FIT note flags he is technically mapped as prominent rather than full lead, but in this small field he is overwhelmingly likely to command the front.|

runners_data.name: Red Happy
runners_data.note: Back just two days after a run, which is the most pressing concern; his one course win came over 24f on Good ground and this 3m1½f trip is his longest assignment yet, so stamina beyond two miles will be tested — a natural prominent type who should have no problem getting his position in this field.|

runners_data.name: Sean Og
runners_data.note: Strong recent form (74-141) with two wins on Good ground make him a live contender on ratings, and Dianne Sayer's 1/6 14-day strike rate confirms the yard is in form; however, he is a natural front-runner who finds himself unable to get his preferred forward berth in this race, forced to sit behind Stratagem and Red Happy — that compromise will need Quinlan to time his run perfectly.|

runners_data.name: Le Malin
runners_data.note: 571 days absent is the dominant flag here — nearly 19 months off the track for a 12-year-old jumping at Cartmel in open handicap company represents a formidable fitness question; he showed a win on Good ground previously but five of his last 11 similar-going starts yielded just one win, and any notable contribution in this spot would be a surprise.|

runners_data.name: Slaney Opera
runners_data.note: Trainer Nick Scholfield is in form (2/10 over 14 days) and tb headgear signals he needs restraining, which is ironic given he is a natural prominent type who cannot get his preferred forward position in this field; his recent form of 3-435F shows modest efforts and a fall, and he must settle into an unnatural midfield role — the style compromise is a meaningful handicap.|

races.paceDynamic: Stratagem is the one confirmed front-runner here and, with only five runners at Cartmel over 3m1½f on Good ground, he is expected to bowl along at the head of affairs unchallenged and set a measured, controlled tempo. Red Happy will press or track from a prominent position, while Sean Og and Slaney Opera are both natural front-runners pushed back into a midfield mapping because there is simply not enough room at the head of affairs for all three prominent types — Stratagem and Red Happy are most likely to actually secure those forward berths, with Sean Og and Slaney Opera compelled to settle in behind their natural position. Le Malin is the one genuine hold-up operator, coming off a 571-day absence and likely to be given even more ground to make up. A sustainable, uncontested gallop set by Stratagem over this stiff staying trip on Good turf strongly favours a prominent racer who gets the rail and travels economically — an honest pace that does not stretch the field sets up a grinding finish where the best traveller wins rather than the sharpest finisher.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Stratagem Controls Throughout
scenarios.trigger: If Stratagem bowls along unchallenged and sets a true but sustainable gallop, allowing him to quicken into the fences and stay on strongly.
scenarios.body: Stratagem leads from the front at a metronomic pace over 3m1½f on Good Cartmel ground, his preferred conditions, and his jockey Mr J P Murray dictates terms without any pressure from rivals; his solid similar-going record (8/15, 3W5P) and two wins over this exact 26f trip underpin his suitability to this shape.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Two Battle It Out
scenarios.trigger: If Red Happy, back just 2 days after a run, travels smoothly and challenges Stratagem from an early stage, turning it into a two-horse duel from the home turn.
scenarios.body: A front-two battle reduces the race to a stamina and jumping contest between Stratagem and Red Happy, with their rivals unable to land a blow from behind; Red Happy's one win over 24f on Good suggests he stays well, though the longer 3m1½f trip and quick turnaround are unknowns.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Racer Pounces Late
scenarios.trigger: If the front two run each other into the ground and Sean Og or Slaney Opera manages to travel more freely than their redistributed map position suggests.
scenarios.body: Sean Og has strong Good-ground form (11/15 similar-going, 2W5P) and is handled by Sean Quinlan who can produce a well-timed challenge if allowed to stride on; however, both Sean Og and Slaney Opera are racing out of their natural role here, making this a discounted shape dependent on things going wrong up front.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Late Closer Lands Blow
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is surprisingly strong early and Le Malin, returning from 571 days off, produces an unexpected burst of form from the back.
scenarios.body: Le Malin has a win over 20f Good ground in his record but a 571-day layoff makes any meaningful contribution highly speculative; this scenario requires the whole field to tire dramatically, which is unlikely given the small field and measured Stratagem-led gallop.

watchPoints.text: Stratagem's lead is entirely unchallenged — if Mr J P Murray (7lb claim) gets him into an easy jumping rhythm from the front, he can win without a serious test and his two previous wins at this exact 26f trip on Good ground are the clearest form line in the race.
Red Happy's 2-day turnaround is highly unusual for a chaser over 3m1½f — watch for any signs of fatigue or jumping errors in the final circuit if he has been raced fresh by design or necessity.

Sean Og and Slaney Opera are both natural front-runners who have been compressed into mid-division by the race shape; if either pulls hard or jumps markedly to get a forward position, it could unsettle the tactical flow even in this small field.

Le Malin's 571-day absence means his jumping sharpness over fences is completely unknown — a significant jumping mistake from him at any point could interfere with the runners immediately behind the leaders on Cartmel's tight track.

Cartmel's undulating, tight course with a run-in that rewards jumping accuracy over sprinting speed means any horse that makes a jumping error at the final fence could hand the initiative to a well-positioned rival — Stratagem's jumping record on similar ground (3W5P in 15 similar-going runs) suggests he is reliable, but watch the last two fences closely.

races.name: Weatherbys Design & Print Novices' Limited Handicap Steeple Chase (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Dunkerque
runners_data.note: Six-year-old with a career-best five wins all on good ground at 20-22f — conditions here are squarely in his wheelhouse; Jennie Candlish's 2/20 14-day strike rate is modest but Dunkerque's own form (91-111) speaks louder, and racing from his natural prominent position means there is no style compromise whatsoever.

runners_data.name: Krak
runners_data.note: Dan and Harry Skelton operate at 6/25 in the 14-day window and are always dangerous in small-field chases; Krak's hold-up style means he depends on others to set a testing pace, and his recent form of 70P-24 — including a pulled-up — raises jumping reliability questions over fences that Cartmel will expose.

runners_data.name: Kientzheim
runners_data.note: Won most recently over 20f on soft and placed over 17f on both soft and good — trips slightly short of today's 2m1½f but Ben Haslam's yard is 1/10 in the 14-day window; Harry Cobden adds class and his natural hold-up style requires a strong enough gallop from the front that may not materialise under Dunkerque's likely stranglehold.

runners_data.name: Heart Above
runners_data.note: A 2-day turnaround is an immediate flag — trainer Dianne Sayer is 1/6 in the 14-day window but running a horse back within 48 hours at a Jumps festival demands scrutiny; one win at 21f good is relevant, though the form string of 97-1P9 reveals more misses than hits and her naturally prominent style could see her chase Dunkerque to her own detriment.

runners_data.name: Passing Diamond
runners_data.note: Strong recent form with back-to-back wins (33-113) and Ben Haslam's yard, sharing Kientzheim, is a trainer double possibility; by instinct this horse wants to race prominently, but with Dunkerque ahead and Heart Above also forward-going, he is likely to find himself tracking further back than ideal, blunting the natural aggression that produced those wins.

races.paceDynamic: Dunkerque is the confirmed front-runner here and, with only Heart Above and Passing Diamond as potential challengers for the lead, he is likely to dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop from the front at Cartmel's tight, turning track. Heart Above's recent form (97-1P9) and a 2-day turnaround suggest she is unlikely to pressurise Dunkerque meaningfully, while Passing Diamond — a genuine front-runner by nature — has been mapped to midfield purely because two other prominent types are ahead of him in the pecking order, meaning this field holds more forward-going horses than can realistically all secure their preferred positions; Dunkerque and Heart Above are likeliest to actually hold the prominent berths. With Krak and Kientzheim operating as hold-up horses from the rear, the race shape points to a steady, front-runner-controlled tempo on good ground at a track that already rewards jumping fluency and positional control. This race shape most favours a well-placed front-runner or close-tracking prominent type who can exploit an uncontested, measured pace and kick away from the last.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Dunkerque Controls From Front
scenarios.trigger: If Dunkerque jumps well and is allowed to dictate an unchallenged, measured gallop throughout
scenarios.body: Dunkerque's recent five-win sequence on good ground at similar distances gives him every right to hold a controlling lead, and Cartmel's tight, undulating circuit amplifies the advantage of a horse settled in front and jumping economically. A calm pace with no sustained pressure means the hold-up horses Krak and Kientzheim face a significant ask to reel him in from off the pace.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Storm Home
scenarios.trigger: If the pace quickens sufficiently in the back straight to string the field out and leave the front pair vulnerable at the last
scenarios.body: Kientzheim showed a 2/17f run on soft and has Harry Cobden in the saddle, giving him tactical nous to time a late run, while Krak with Harry Skelton is also capable of producing a telling late burst if the gallop lifts. Both true hold-up horses would need Dunkerque to have set a testing enough pace to leave him vulnerable on the run-in at Cartmel's short finishing stretch.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Type Outstays
scenarios.trigger: If Dunkerque makes an error or fades and a mid-pack mover swoops to lead turning in
scenarios.body: Passing Diamond — a natural front-runner in reality who has been forced to track from midfield — could capitalise if he recovers his true position on a mistake by the leader, and his form of 33-113 includes back-to-back wins at 20f on good ground. Heart Above's one win at 21f on good ground is also relevant, though a 2-day turnaround and inconsistent form dampen confidence.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Attrition Chaos Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If multiple fallers or a rash of jumping errors create a chaotic, ragged race that negates positional advantages
scenarios.body: In a small five-runner field over fences, any carnage at fences would disproportionately benefit whichever horse is jumping cleanly and tracks close enough to inherit the lead. This is a low-probability scenario but Kientzheim's clean jumping record and Cobden's experience could make him the unlikely beneficiary.

watchPoints.text: Dunkerque jumps the last fence cleanly — if he pings it and has even a length advantage on the run-in, Cartmel's tight finish gives chasers almost no room to reel him in.
Heart Above's 2-day turnaround is unusual in a chase context — watch her in the paddock for sweat or signs of residual fatigue before inferring she can replicate her one win at this trip.

Passing Diamond is likely to race out of his natural role due to the congestion up front — if he is seen fighting for position in the early stages, energy expenditure before the fences begin could compromise his finish.

Krak's jumping record includes a pulled-up run — watch the first three fences for any signs of hesitation or awkwardness; a mistake at Cartmel's tight-turning fences can cost lengths with no room to recover.

The Skelton combination (Krak) and Cobden (Kientzheim) both have the tactical ability to manufacture a prominent position if the pace is slower than expected — monitor the first circuit for either drifting closer than their starting style suggests.

races.paceDynamic: Kingofthegame is the sole confirmed front-runner here and, with Ryan Mania aboard, is expected to bowl along from the outset and control tempo over 2m5f on Good ground at Cartmel — a track that rewards horses who can travel economically and jump fluently. With just one horse setting the pace, the gallop will likely be honest but not suicidal, creating a race that unfolds in a relatively strung-out, single-file manner rather than dissolving into a bunched sprint. The field contains a heavy concentration of genuine hold-up horses — Wearelongterm, Blazing Court, Aill Dubh, and Fast Deal are all natural rear-division types redistributed into the midfield section of the map simply because there are too many closers to place honestly at the back — meaning the real contest will be decided by who can travel prominently or make smooth headway from mid-division rather than from deep. This race shape strongly favours prominently-ridden horses who can sit just off the pace and mount a measured challenge from the third-last, with the clean-travelling prominent types (Path Of Stars, Judicial Review) and the better-class hold-up horses capable of picking through a congested midfield (Imperial Rule, El Muchacho) the profiles to focus on.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Kingofthegame Controls Throughout
scenarios.trigger: If Kingofthegame dictates an uncontested lead and the field strings out behind without major pressure.
scenarios.body: Kingofthegame, trained by Martin Todhunter and riding in form having won twice over this C&D trip, sets a sustainable gallop that suits horses who can track fluently and pounce from the second-last; with no genuine challenger for the lead, the race becomes a test of jumping accuracy and jumping at pace rather than raw acceleration.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Stalkers Overhaul Leader
scenarios.trigger: If Kingofthegame's pace proves just too strong late and the closest trackers (Path Of Stars, Judicial Review) wear him down from the third-last.
scenarios.body: Path Of Stars, a five-year-old with solid Good-ground form and an excellent RPR for this class, is ideally suited to tracking a lone leader and producing a clean late challenge; Judicial Review, similarly prominent in style, can benefit from the same shape if Leah Noreci settles him handy early.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Thread Through
scenarios.trigger: If Kingofthegame fades sharply from two out and the midfield compresses, allowing the classier hold-up horses to pick their way through.
scenarios.body: Imperial Rule (OR 100, three wins at around this trip on Good ground) has the form profile to take advantage if a gap opens in a tiring field, and El Muchacho's consistent placing record on Good ground makes him a natural beneficiary of a late scramble.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Race Falls Apart, Attrition Wins
scenarios.trigger: If jumping errors or the Cartmel terrain cause early casualties and the field thins dramatically, handing the advantage to a staying-type who simply completes cleanly.
scenarios.body: A messy, strung-out race with fallers or pulled-up horses opens the door for a relentless stayer who conserves energy from midfield; Jack Sprat and Aill Dubh, both proven at this sort of distance on Good ground, could capitalise simply by keeping their feet.

watchPoints.text: Kingofthegame is the race-shaper — if Ryan Mania is taken on early or the horse jumps poorly at the first fence it could unravel the dominant pace scenario entirely and scramble the entire field.

Wearelongterm, Blazing Court and Aill Dubh are all genuine closers crammed into what will effectively be a congested middle group; watch for traffic problems and interference at the downhill fences unique to Cartmel's undulating layout.

Fast Deal carries the ⚠ fades-in-finish flag and is lowest-rated — its presence in midfield rather than safely at the rear means it could cause crowding issues or be a jumping liability for those behind it from the fourth fence onward.

Path Of Stars is a five-year-old making only his second start at this distance; if Benjamin Macey misjudges the pace and advances too soon over Cartmel's sharp track, the horse could find the last half-mile beyond him despite strong Good-ground form credentials.

Three runners — Kingofthegame, Wearelongterm, and Judicial Review — all ran within the last two days; monitor any market drifts at the off as trainer intentions around recovery may not be fully priced in.
